subject: Discovery summary + next steps — technical acceptance metrics & test plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@findata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery summary + next steps — technical acceptance metrics & test plan

Hi Olivia —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and the hands-on evaluation plan we discussed. I’ve kept this tight so we can lock next steps.

1) Top pain points you shared
- Inference cost at scale: current per‑token spend on hosted API varies significantly with burst traffic and is unpredictable for batch scoring jobs.
- Tail latency & SLOs: model responses exceed user-facing latency budgets during peak windows (p99 ~ 2.8s for interactive flows).
- Model drift & governance: tight auditability required for risk teams; retention and KV cache controls needed.

2) Current stack
- Primary: Managed cloud endpoints (vendor: CloudGenAI) for chat + reranking; some local GPU pools for offline batch scoring (NVIDIA A10).
- Orchestration: In-house router controls traffic between cloud endpoints and on-prem pools.
- Observability: Mix of Prometheus + Sentry; token cost mapping is ad‑hoc in BI.

3) Success criteria for a proof-of-evaluation (POE)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms for interactive prompt sizes ~512 tokens.
- Throughput: sustained 250 RPS for 1k token average batch within reserved capacity.
- Cost: target token-unit cost reduction >= 25% vs current CloudGenAI baseline for production mix (chat + reranking).
- Quality parity: end-to-end output quality within acceptable delta on the provided eval set (we captured fidelity checks in the attached template).
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown and audit logs for every request.

4) Proposed evaluation assets we need from FinData
- Representative request set (CSV): ~5k rows spanning short chat, 1–2 prompt templates for reranking, and 500 long prompts for batch scoring.
- Success metrics weighting (see attached redwood_eval_template.csv).
- A small synthetic peak profile: 300 RPS sustained for 10 minutes followed by 800 RPS bursts (for stress runs).

5) Our deliverables for the POE (what Redwood will run)
- Dedicated eval window (2 weeks) with a pinned model variant and telemetry access.
- Baseline runs vs CloudGenAI (your production), plus two internal variants: quantized optimization and KV-caching enabled.
- Detailed report: latency distributions, cost per token, throughput, failure modes, and recommended runtime settings.

6) Preliminary schedule (provisional)
- By Tue 4/14: FinData sends the representative request set + weighting.
- Week of 4/20: Redwood config & smoke runs.
- Week of 4/27: Full comparison runs + final report.

7) Risks & asks
- If you have any NDAs / procurement constraints, please flag early so our legal can triage.
- For accurate cost parity we need an example CloudGenAI billing slice (anonymized is fine).

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.csv (evaluation metric mapping), rdw_trial-config.yaml (example trial config we’ll use).

Next steps: if that looks right I’ll send a short HubSpot invite with the proposed POE dates and loop in our infra lead (Marissa) for the smoke-run kickoff.

Thanks again — excited to help tighten your inference economics.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Park <olivia@findata.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery summary + next steps — technical acceptance metrics & test plan

Thanks Rafael — the recap is great and captures everything we discussed. A couple clarifications from the FinData engineering side: 

- The production CloudGenAI baseline numbers I referred to are for the mixed chat + rerank workload (monthly 40M tokens). Happy to provide an anonymized billing export — I’ll attach that to the dataset we share.
- For quality parity we care most about reranker NDCG@10 and a small set of customer-facing hallucination checks (we’ll annotate ~200 prompts).
- On schedule: the dataset and preference weights are on track for 4/14. Our legal has a standard data processing addendum; I’ll send that over if you need it.

We’re also curious about your comparison methodology vs vLLM/TGI. Can you confirm which flavors you’ll run as part of the POE? We’d like to ensure we’re comparing equivalent quantization/float settings.

– Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Platform Engineering | FinData Inc
olivia@findata.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@findata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery summary + next steps — technical acceptance metrics & test plan

Great — thanks for the quick replies, Olivia. A few specifics so there’s no ambiguity on what we’ll run: 

- Comparison matrix:
  * CloudGenAI (your production config) — we’ll ask for your anonymized billing slice and production prompt mix so we can replay similar traffic.
  * vLLM baseline — unoptimized open runtime, default FP32 weights where possible.
  * TGI baseline — standard TGI serving config with your model architecture mapped (we’ll use the community TGI docker image unless you prefer otherwise).
  * Redwood variants: 1) quantization-optimized (8-bit) runtime, 2) KV-caching + prefix caching enabled.

- Important: for fairness we’ll attempt to match model precisions and max_seq/kv settings. Where exact parity isn’t possible we’ll note the delta and include accuracy/throughput tradeoffs in the final report.

- Acceptance thresholds (from your earlier notes + our suggestions): p95 < 450ms; sustained 200–300 RPS for 1k token average; cost improvement >= 25% vs anonymized CloudGenAI baseline; NDCG delta <= 0.02 on the annotated reranker set.

I’ll attach a short config file (rdw_trial-config.yaml) that contains the environment variables and measurement hooks we use. Marissa — could you coordinate the smoke-run (est. 2 hours) once FinData shares the CSV? Sean — want to own the replay infra and ensure the right telemetry tags are present?

Olivia — once you send the dataset I’ll create the HubSpot POE record and we’ll lock the test window.

Thanks,
— Rafael
